requirement:
For a definition-name mapping, `habeas refactor` MUST rewrite each `{impl}`,
`{test}`, `{cite}`, `{fixme}`, and `{term}` reference that names an old name,
in the book and in the sources reference discovery considers. For a path or
node mapping, it MUST rewrite each `:impl:` or `:test:` anchor that names an
old file or node. It MUST change nothing else in those files.
rationale:
structural: Every clause of `requirements.refactor.reference_rewrite` states observable behavior, so none creates a structural obligation. The node has no Implements edges and no review roots were supplied, so there is nothing to inspect. I checked each candidate clause for an alternative implementation that gives the same results but breaks the clause:
- "`habeas refactor` MUST rewrite each `{impl}`, `{test}`, `{cite}`, `{fixme}`, and `{term}` reference that names an old name": this describes which references end up rewritten. An implementation could use a regex pass, a parser, or any other method and produce the same file contents.
- "in the book and in the sources reference discovery considers": this defines the set of files affected. It does not say the code must call a particular discovery function. A separate scanner that visits the same files would behave identically, so reuse of discovery is discretionary.
- "rewrite each `:impl:` or `:test:` anchor that names an old file or node": this is the same kind of output-only rule for path and node mappings.
- "MUST change nothing else in those files": this limits what the output may contain. It prescribes no type, library, signature, or delegation.
The text names no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or interface. No implementation root needs a reference, and tests can cover the behavior.

behavioral: All three obligations of `requirements.refactor.reference_rewrite` have marked tests that assert the outcome.

**Name mapping rewrites `{impl}`, `{test}`, `{cite}`, `{fixme}` and `{term}` references, in the book and in sources.**
- `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[sources_rewrite_references_to_names_and_anchors_to_paths]` maps `rules.check` to `core.check`. It asserts that `{impl}` and a fenced `:::{fixme}` in a Rust source are rewritten. It also asserts that `{term}` in Markdown is rewritten.
- The same test leaves `{cite}`rules.checker`` unchanged. That is a different name, so it shows only exact old names are rewritten.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_requirement_renames_its_references_and_evidence]` checks `{cite}` in the book (`md/notes.md`). It also checks `{impl}` and `{test}` in `src/config.rs`.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_term_rewrites_definition_inputs_and_the_texts_using_it]` checks `{term}` in the book, in `md/usage.md`.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_rename_rewrites_the_hash_of_a_node_whose_doc_comment_names_it]` checks `{impl}` in a doc comment.

**Path and node mappings rewrite `:impl:` and `:test:` anchors.**
- The unit test rewrites `:impl: data.txt` to `info.txt`. It rewrites `:test: data.txt#line@abc` to `info.txt#line@abc`, so a node anchor inside a moved file is covered.
- `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_file_rewrites_anchors_and_paths]` runs the whole command and asserts that `md/rules.md` now has `:impl: info.txt`.
- `src/refactor/tests.rs#fn[anchors_follow_a_node_mapping_and_leave_other_nodes_alone]` covers node mappings. It asserts that exactly one anchor changes, from `src/a.rs#fn[f]` to `src/b.rs#fn[g]`. It also asserts that `:test: src/a.rs#fn[other]` is untouched.

**It changes nothing else.**
- The unit test leaves the declaration name `other` unchanged.
- It leaves a `{cite}` inside a code block literal.
- It leaves option-like lines in body text or code blocks literal, with 0 edits.
- It leaves a role inside a string literal unchanged.
- It leaves `:impl:` in a plain `.txt` file unchanged.
- The integration tests compare snapshots of the whole project. `a_moved_requirement_renames_its_references_and_evidence` asserts that only the expected files changed, which are the rewritten sources, the book note and the evidence files. `a_moved_file_rewrites_anchors_and_paths` asserts that, after excluding the evidence record, the other files equal the expected snapshot with only the anchor changed. Together these show that a name mapping leaves anchors unchanged and a path mapping leaves references unchanged.

I read `rewrite_source` in `src/refactor.rs` only to see which file kinds it handles. The expected behavior above comes from the requirement text, and the tests cover each branch the text distinguishes. I found no behavioral gap.
